product_from_film: Venice presents itself as private, unrestricted AI that protects a person’s ideas.
explains_well: A visitor photographing another person’s chalkboard makes the idea-theft concern tangible.
unclear: No AI interface, user task or technical privacy mechanism is shown.
scenario: A researcher’s work is photographed and marked by another person, used as a metaphor for idea appropriation.
product_clear_basis: The closing descriptor Private, Unrestricted AI first appears at 26s.

categories.finding: The photographing action and final claim establish the metaphor silently. The actual AI service is only named in the final descriptor.
The wide board establishes scale; closer facial and shoulder views shift attention to the visitor’s phone and writing hand.
The film carries one metaphor with very little text. It leaves ample time for the action but almost none for practical product explanation.
The opening establishes authored work; the intrusion and privacy claim pay off that concern. There is no demonstrated product solution.
The glasses and face gesture suggest effort or fatigue; the intruder is framed to provoke unease. These are interpretations, not established feelings.
categories.reason: Actor state and viewer response are not independently known.

categories.finding: One board and two people stay in the same room throughout, making the metaphor easy to follow.
Private, unrestricted AI is a claim. The staged action supplies a metaphor and no evidence of data handling.
The chalkboard metaphor is memorable, but without the final name and AI line it could advertise other privacy products.
Every shot advances one intrusion story. A short real privacy control after the claim would add practical proof.
categories.experiment: Append one clearly labeled product control rather than adding more metaphor.

categories.finding: For Tin ownership messaging, use one campaign draft being copied as a short metaphor, then show an actual sharing/access control.
categories.experiment: Keep the metaphor under ten seconds and prove the setting in a real UI state.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Use one concrete physical action to explain an abstract data concern.
try: For Tin access controls, show a campaign draft being copied, then cut to the exact permission setting that controls sharing.
Test an opening on the phone photographing the board, followed by the owner reaction and product claim, to shorten time to the central issue.
lessons.avoid: Treating a privacy metaphor as evidence of actual privacy protection.
lessons.open: Actual privacy behavior, scene production method, sound and audience interpretation remain unverified.

comparison.story: Researcher and work → intrusive photographing/marking → privacy claim.
